VERDICT.headline: ZERO of the d_seg gap is render-side-reachable POST-HOC. All 3 render-side levers HURT d_seg on the l7-best ckpt (n600): AA +0.00163 (+49%), analytic-lane +0.00082 (+25%), both +0.00213 (+64%).
VERDICT.mechanism_aa: Box-filtering the witness OWN sharp synthetic palette edges blurs thin lane markings -> SegNet erases MORE lanes (lane_recall 0.758->0.656, lane_fn 0.00136->0.00194). AA recovers UNDERSAMPLED real detail; it degrades OVERSAMPLED synthetic renders.
VERDICT.mechanism_lane: The analytic band adds net FALSE-POSITIVE lane pixels (lane_fp 0.00060->0.00115, ~2x) from dash-gap leakage + fit error (band-vs-GT-lane recall only 0.639) that outweigh the tiny recall gain (0.758->0.767). Matches FEED-dj dash-gap-FP finding.
VERDICT.root_cause: The witness OVERFIT its EXACT render pipeline (point-sample @384 -> contest R). Any post-hoc render change (AA / composite) moves OFF the training distribution -> d_seg rises.
VERDICT.implication_221: The 0.0033->0.001 islands gap requires RETRAINING that changes the learned field, NOT a cheap post-hoc render-side patch. Fine-tune-FIRST is favored (0.0033 is a strong init) BUT the render-side levers (AA / analytic-lane) must be trained INTO the render+loss jointly (fine-tune with the new render ACTIVE), never bolted on post-hoc. This is the -render-side levers need the boundaries re-adapted- branch.
VERDICT.sanity: c1=0.00333 = byte-closeable deployment render (self-checked byte-identical to decode_levelset_torch). ~0.0007 below the trainer in-loop best 0.004024 (levelset_best.json) = the documented self-orient fixed-point reconstruction gap (close-but-not-bit-identical), not a bug. Correct ~0.003-0.004 regime.
